<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Image source and pre-filtering.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use SA-1B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kirillov et al., 2023</a>)</cite> as the sole image source.
Before any model call, we keep only images whose longer side has at least 1280 pixels, whose mean per-channel intensity entropy is at least 6.5 bits, whose Canny edge density is at least 0.04, and whose luminance standard deviation is at least 60.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Grounded evidence discovery.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each image, a single call with the image and its caption (Prompt <a href="#A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" title="Prompt B.1: Grounded region inventory ‣ B.1 Evidence Discovery and Question Construction ‣ Appendix B Prompt Templates for EvidenceConnect ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>) judges whether the image can support multi-region questions and returns up to 18 region proposals, whose box coordinates are converted to pixels and clamped to the image.
We then discard boxes that cover less than 0.04% or more than 18% of the image, as well as boxes whose IoU with an earlier kept box is at least 0.65.
Images judged unsuitable, or with fewer than four remaining regions, are skipped.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Task-conditioned evidence grouping.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A text-only call receives the caption together with the label and local description of each region, ranked by grounding confidence (Prompt <a href="#A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2" title="Prompt B.2: Task-conditioned region-group proposal ‣ B.1 Evidence Discovery and Question Construction ‣ Appendix B Prompt Templates for EvidenceConnect ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>), and proposes up to six groups of 3–7 regions.
Each group is annotated with one of 22 task families, which map to four necessity modes that refine the three question forms of Section <a href="#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" title="Target question structure. ‣ 3.1 Multi-region Question Synthesis ‣ 3 Boosting Multimodal Perception by Learning to Connect Visual Evidence ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>.
Specifically, <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">answer_sensitive</span> covers aggregation (counting, numeric aggregation, and arithmetic), <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">set_complete</span> (filtering, anomaly, extremum, matching, and geometric, topological, or depth relations) and <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">pair_complete</span> (cross-region pairing) cover comparison and matching, and <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chain_dependency</span> (OCR, spatial, viewpoint, conditional, Boolean, relational, and multi-hop chains) covers dependency chains and compositions.
We keep groups whose region identifiers are valid, whose size lies in the allowed range, and that do not repeat an earlier group.
In addition, the candidates of a filtering, anomaly, or extremum group must not mix coarse semantic classes, and groups with distinct task families are kept before groups that repeat a family.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Privileged evidence layout.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each region is cropped at native resolution with a margin of 8% of its box size on every side.
The crops are placed on a white canvas through an order-preserving remapping of each image axis, which removes the rows and columns not covered by any crop, and the canvas is uniformly downscaled only when its longer side exceeds 4096 pixels.
Each region receives a distinct color from a seven-color palette, which bounds the group size at seven.
The same colors are used in the question text, in the privileged and ablated layouts, and for the outlines on the marked policy view.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Question realization.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each group, the generator receives the privileged layout, the group metadata (labels, local descriptions, natural referents, box coordinates, and outline colors), four blueprints sampled from a library of 104 reasoning templates, and up to four additional free-form slots, and it returns up to eight candidates (Prompt <a href="#A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3" title="Prompt B.3: Privileged question and certificate realization ‣ B.1 Evidence Discovery and Question Construction ‣ Appendix B Prompt Templates for EvidenceConnect ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>).
The first blueprint follows the proposed task family when possible, and the remaining ones diversify answer forms and question types.
Each candidate declares its question type, necessity mode, answer semantics (scalar, unordered set, or ordered pair), answer kind (outline color, number, Boolean pattern, semantic phrase, text, semantic set, or semantic pair), the contribution of every region, the predicted answer after removing each region, and a reasoning certificate.
Open-vocabulary answers must contain fewer than ten words.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Rule-based checks and candidate selection.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A certificate is valid only if every step reads from earlier steps alone, every selected region lies on a path to the output step, and no step is disconnected from it.
Aggregation, arithmetic, and Boolean questions must further use an executable certificate with a restricted operator set.
For aggregation questions, every region must receive a positive value, and the values must sum to the answer without all being one, since the answer would otherwise equal the number of outlined regions.
Similarly, arithmetic expressions must reference every region and evaluate to the answer.
We further reject candidates that expose region identifiers, do not refer to the marked regions, use conditional wording without explicit branches or outside conditional types, count vague background targets, request more than one output for a scalar answer, omit an explicit coordinate frame for spatial types, leak the answer through an outline color, use subjective phrasing, or declare an answer form that the answer does not match.
Candidates whose own predicted answer after removing some region equals their proposed answer are rejected as well.
The remaining candidates are ranked by the generator’s self-assessed naturalness, visual confidence, and multi-region scores, with bonuses for compositional types and non-numeric answers, and this ranking only determines which candidates proceed to verification.
Per group, we keep up to four top-ranked candidates, preferring distinct question types and allowing at most one numeric and two outline-color answers.
Per image, we keep up to eight candidates but always retain the best candidate of each question type.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cross-model answer anchoring.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each candidate is answered on the privileged layout by both anchoring families, with up to four samples per family and without the region descriptions or the generator’s answer (Prompt <a href="#A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" title="Prompt B.4: Privileged-view answer anchoring ‣ B.2 Answer Anchoring and Dependency Checks ‣ Appendix B Prompt Templates for EvidenceConnect ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>).
For closed-form questions, the prompt also lists the allowed answer labels, and we first draw two samples per family.
Such a candidate is rejected early unless at least three of these four responses agree and each family contributes at least one of them.
Responses are clustered by normalized string matching with numeric equivalence, and if the largest cluster has fewer than six members, the text-only judge re-clusters all responses by semantic equivalence (Prompt <a href="#A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2" title="Prompt B.5: Semantic-equivalence clustering ‣ B.2 Answer Anchoring and Dependency Checks ‣ Appendix B Prompt Templates for EvidenceConnect ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>).
A candidate is accepted if the largest cluster is not an insufficiency response and contains at least three of the four responses from each family, and its answer then becomes <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Finally, <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is re-checked against the answer-form constraints above.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px8" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Adaptive drop-one testing.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each selected region, its crop in the privileged layout is replaced by a gray block with a red cross, while all other crops stay in place.
The first anchoring family answers each ablated view once, with a mode-specific addendum to the answering prompt (Prompt <a href="#A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3" title="Prompt B.6: Mode-specific drop-one verification ‣ B.2 Answer Anchoring and Dependency Checks ‣ Appendix B Prompt Templates for EvidenceConnect ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>).
If the response matches <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> or cannot be parsed, the same view is queried twice more, and the region is redundant if at least two of its three responses match <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>.
A candidate is rejected if two or more of its regions are redundant.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px9" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Policy view.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unmarked rewriting is attempted only for aggregate question types (object counts, attribute counts, and sums of visible numbers), whose answers do not depend on the outlines, whereas the answers of selection and pairing questions are often outline colors themselves.
The first anchoring family rewrites the question for the unmarked image and proposes distractors (Prompt <a href="#A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1" title="Prompt B.7: Unmarked-question rewrite ‣ B.3 Policy-View and Multiple-Choice Construction ‣ Appendix B Prompt Templates for EvidenceConnect ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>), and rewrites that still mention boxes or outlines are discarded.
Two audits from each family (Prompt <a href="#A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2" title="Prompt B.8: Independent audit of the unmarked rewrite ‣ B.3 Policy-View and Multiple-Choice Construction ‣ Appendix B Prompt Templates for EvidenceConnect ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>) must then all report unique references, task preservation, identifiable targets, multi-region dependence, and necessity of every evidence area.
Each audit must also recover <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> and ground exactly one box per intended region, and the grounded boxes must match the intended regions one-to-one, where a grounded box matches a region if its center lies inside the region’s box enlarged by 15%.
Otherwise, the example keeps the marked policy view, on which the box of each selected region is outlined in its assigned color.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px10" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multiple-choice conversion.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px10.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For marked examples, the first anchoring family proposes three distractors given the marked image, the question, and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> (Prompt <a href="#A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3" title="Prompt B.9: Multiple-choice distractor generation ‣ B.3 Policy-View and Multiple-Choice Construction ‣ Appendix B Prompt Templates for EvidenceConnect ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>), whereas unmarked examples reuse the distractors from the rewrite step.
We remove empty distractors, distractors that match <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> after normalization, duplicates, and, for closed-form answers, options outside the label vocabulary.
If fewer than three distractors remain, we fill the missing options deterministically, for example with alternative subsets of set-valued answers, unused vocabulary labels, or neighboring integers for count answers.
The four options are then shuffled, and the prompt asks for the option letter.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px11" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Difficulty filtering.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px11.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The screening model answers each example four times on its policy view (Prompt <a href="#A2.SS3.SSS0.Px4" title="Prompt B.10: Difficulty sampling on the policy view ‣ B.3 Policy-View and Multiple-Choice Construction ‣ Appendix B Prompt Templates for EvidenceConnect ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>).
Examples with four correct responses or any unparseable response are discarded, and the remaining ones are labeled easy, medium, hard, or very hard when three, two, one, or none of the responses are correct.
Finally, we keep at most four examples per source image, and each training example consists of the policy view and the multiple-choice question.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Prompt Templates for <span id="A2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">EvidenceConnect</span></h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section lists the prompt templates used by <span id="A2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">EvidenceConnect</span>.
We replace instance-specific values with angle-bracketed placeholders and condense long templates for readability.
Specifically, we keep their task definitions, key constraints, and main output fields, and omit examples, formatting reminders, repeated instructions, and fields unused in our setting.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Evidence Discovery and Question Construction</h3>

<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompt B.1: Grounded region inventory</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><pre id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
[IMAGE]
You are a precise visual grounding annotator and data-quality gate.

Task: Decide whether this image can support natural questions whose
answer genuinely depends on 3--7 distinct regions, then propose up to
&lt;MAX_REGIONS&gt; useful evidence regions.

Image caption, if available: &lt;IMAGE_CAPTION&gt;

Return regions that are:
- visually concrete and clearly localizable;
- useful for multi-region reasoning, including people, animals, objects,
signs, screens, text regions, fine details, and distinctive parts;
- preferably small or medium-sized, spatially diverse, and not overly
overlapping;
- suitable for coherent tasks such as positive-contribution counting,
closed-set filtering, anomaly/extremum detection, candidate matching,
pairing, OCR--visual verification, or a short dependent spatial chain.

Prioritize groups of related regions over isolated interesting objects.
The image is suitable only if at least one coherent all-region task is
possible. Avoid vague regions such as "background," "scene," "sky,"
"room," or the whole image.

For each region, return:
- label: short name;
- bbox: [x1,y1,x2,y2] in pixels, or normalized 0--1000 coordinates;
- caption: one concise visible description;
- natural_referent: an identifying phrase without coordinates or IDs;
- role: candidate | reference | comparator | text_region |
      count_target | fine_part | distractor;
- confidence: grounding confidence.

Return JSON only:
{
"suitable_for_multi_region_vqa": true,
"richness_reason": "...",
"coherent_sets": [
  {"labels": [...], "task_family": "..."}
],
"regions": [
  {
    "label": "...", "bbox": [...], "caption": "...",
    "natural_referent": "...", "role": "...", "confidence": 0.0
  }
]
}
</pre>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompt B.2: Task-conditioned region-group proposal</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><pre id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
You are an expert VQA data curator. Below are &lt;N&gt; candidate evidence
regions detected in one image.

Image caption: &lt;IMAGE_CAPTION&gt;
Regions:
- &lt;REGION_ID&gt;: label=&lt;LABEL&gt;; caption=&lt;LOCAL_CAPTION&gt;
- ...

Propose up to &lt;MAX_GROUPS&gt; combinations that are good for natural
questions requiring many regions. A good combination is a coherent
candidate/evidence set, not a bag of unrelated boxes. Prefer the
largest valid set, but every selected region must have a real role.

Allowed task families and necessity modes:
- answer_sensitive: aggregate_count, aggregate_attribute_count,
aggregate_numeric, arithmetic_composition;
- set_complete: set_filtering, anomaly_detection, extremum,
candidate_matching, geometric_line_relation, topological_relation,
depth_ordering;
- pair_complete: cross_region_pairing;
- chain_dependency: ocr_visual_verification, spatial_chain,
dependent_chain, viewpoint_transform, agent_relative_direction,
spatial_transitivity, conditional_composition, boolean_composition,
relational_composition, multi_hop_reasoning.

Selection rules:
1. Select 3--7 regions and prefer larger groups only when coherent.
2. Every region must change an aggregate, belong to the closed
 candidate/pair set, or supply an indispensable chain constraint.
3. Prefer objective text, numbers, countable objects, repeated classes,
 comparable parts, and unambiguous attributes.
4. Filtering, anomaly, and extremum candidates must be comparable.
5. Every aggregate-count region must contribute a positive count.
6. Spatial spread is preferred, but coherence has priority.
7. Diversify task families and do not default to counting.
8. Skip the image if no valid combination exists.

Return JSON only:
[
{
  "region_ids": ["r000", "r001", "r003"],
  "task_family": "anomaly_detection",
  "necessity_mode": "set_complete",
  "reason": "short objective rationale"
}
]
</pre>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompt B.3: Privileged question and certificate realization</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><pre id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
[PRIVILEGED LAYOUT WITH K COLOR-OUTLINED CROPS]
Create &lt;NUM_QUESTIONS&gt; diverse multi-region VQA questions.

Scope contract:
- The selected set is exactly &lt;REGION_IDS&gt;.
- Every question must genuinely use all K regions.
- evidence_region_ids, region_contributions, answer_if_dropped, and
the reasoning certificate must cover exactly this set.
- Never add decorative observations for otherwise unused regions.
- Questions must be answerable from visible pixels in this layout,
not from region captions.

Visible crop anchors (the same outline colors appear on the marked image):
- &lt;REGION_ID&gt;: label=&lt;LABEL&gt;; outline_color=&lt;COLOR&gt;; bbox=&lt;BBOX&gt;;
  caption=&lt;LOCAL_CAPTION&gt;; natural_referent=&lt;REFERENT&gt;
- ...

Task guidance:
- Preferred task family: &lt;TASK_FAMILY&gt;.
- Preferred necessity mode: &lt;NECESSITY_MODE&gt;.
- Selected reasoning blueprints: &lt;TEMPLATE_SPECS&gt;.
- Instantiate a blueprint only when its facts are objectively visible.
- Include diverse closed-set, comparison/matching, OCR/spatial/
relational, and compositional structures.
- Prefer select-then-report questions in which several regions identify
a target and a second visible property supplies the final answer.
- Keep the answer short, objective, unique, and absent from the stem.

Necessity contract:
- answer_sensitive: every region contributes a positive value, so
masking it changes the result or makes the aggregate unknown.
- set_complete / pair_complete: all regions form the explicitly closed
candidate or pairing set; masking one prevents proving completeness.
- chain_dependency: every region supplies an indispensable clue or hop.
- For every region, answer_if_dropped must differ from the reference
answer or be "insufficient information."

Certificate contract:
- First design a natural question from pixels; then provide its
certificate. Do not verbalize the certificate mechanically.
- Use mode="executable" for deterministic reading, counting, filtering,
matching, comparison, arithmetic, Boolean, and lookup programs.
- Use mode="evidence_graph" for open-vocabulary semantic or unusual
multi-hop reasoning.
- Every step has id, op, regions, inputs, and query.
- Inputs may reference only earlier steps.
- Every selected region must lie on a path to output_step.
- No disconnected or decorative step is allowed.

Wording contract:
- Ask for one final answer.
- Use one explicit coordinate frame for spatial questions.
- Use outline colors only as reference anchors, never as leaked object
attributes.
- Open answers must be objective and fewer than 10 words.
- Do not use subjective comparisons, vague counts, or invisible facts.

Return JSON only, one object per candidate:
[
{
  "template_id": "...",
  "question": "...",
  "question_type": "...",
  "necessity_mode": "answer_sensitive | set_complete |
                     pair_complete | chain_dependency",
  "answer_semantics": "scalar | unordered_set | ordered_pair",
  "final_answer_kind": "anchor | numeric | boolean | semantic |
                        semantic_set | semantic_pair | text",
  "evidence_region_ids": [...],
  "region_contributions": {"r000": "...", "...": "..."},
  "region_values": {"r000": 0},
  "aggregation": "...",
  "operation_expression": "...",
  "candidate_region_ids": [...],
  "closed_candidate_set": true,
  "pair_region_ids": [[...], ...],
  "chain_region_ids": [...],
  "coordinate_frame": "image_plane | camera | agent | object |
                       scene_3d | not_applicable",
  "answer_vocabulary": [...],
  "answer_if_dropped": {"r000": "...", "...": "..."},
  "hypothetical_answer": "...",
  "reasoning_certificate": {
    "mode": "executable | evidence_graph",
    "steps": [
      {"id": "s1", "op": "...", "regions": ["r000"],
       "inputs": [], "query": "..."}
    ],
    "output_step": "..."
  },
  "naturalness_score": 1,
  "visual_confidence": 1,
  "multi_region_score": 1
}
]
</pre>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Answer Anchoring and Dependency Checks</h3>

<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompt B.4: Privileged-view answer anchoring</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><pre id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
[PRIVILEGED LAYOUT]
Answer the question using only the provided image.

Question: &lt;QUESTION&gt;
Allowed canonical answer labels: &lt;OPTIONAL_NEUTRAL_VOCABULARY&gt;

You may reason briefly before answering. Put only the final short answer
inside &lt;answer&gt;...&lt;/answer&gt;.

Rules:
- Use an objectively supported expression of fewer than 10 words.
- Use Arabic digits for numbers, with no units or separators.
- Do not emit coordinates, grounding tokens, or box markers.
- Use the same language as the question.
- If evidence is insufficient, output
&lt;answer&gt;insufficient information&lt;/answer&gt;.
- The answer tag is required; responses without it are discarded.
</pre>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompt B.5: Semantic-equivalence clustering</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><pre id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
You are an answer-equivalence judge for a VQA task.

Question: &lt;QUESTION&gt;
Answers:
A1: &lt;ANSWER_1&gt;
...
AN: &lt;ANSWER_N&gt;

Group answers by semantic equivalence. Equivalent paraphrases belong
together; answers with different values, attributes, or truth values
must remain separate.

Return strict JSON only:
{
"groups": [["&lt;CANONICAL_FORM&gt;", [&lt;ANSWER_INDICES&gt;]], ...],
"largest_group_size": &lt;INTEGER&gt;,
"canonical": "&lt;CANONICAL_FORM_OF_LARGEST_GROUP&gt;"
}

Every answer must occur in exactly one group. Break size ties using the
lexicographically smallest canonical form.
</pre>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompt B.6: Mode-specific drop-one verification</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The drop-one verifier inserts one of the following addenda into
Prompt <a href="#A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" title="Prompt B.4: Privileged-view answer anchoring ‣ B.2 Answer Anchoring and Dependency Checks ‣ Appendix B Prompt Templates for EvidenceConnect ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>, depending on the necessity mode.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><pre id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
[answer_sensitive]
ABLATION VIEW: one required aggregate region has been replaced by a
gray masked box. If the full aggregate cannot be computed, answer
"insufficient information"; do not count only visible boxes.

[set_complete or pair_complete]
ABLATION VIEW: one colored candidate box has been replaced by a gray
masked box. The masked box remains a member of the explicitly closed
candidate/pairing set. If its hidden content prevents proving the
complete subset, unique anomaly, global extremum, unique match, or
complete pairing, answer "insufficient information."

[chain_dependency]
ABLATION VIEW: one required clue region has been replaced by a gray
masked box. If the missing clue breaks the reasoning chain, answer
"insufficient information"; do not guess.
</pre>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Policy-View and Multiple-Choice Construction</h3>

<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompt B.7: Unmarked-question rewrite</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><pre id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
[UNMARKED ORIGINAL IMAGE]
You are given an anchored visual question and its verified answer.

Anchored question: &lt;QUESTION&gt;
Verified answer: &lt;ANSWER&gt;

Create a minimally changed question that works on the unmarked image.
Replace box/outline references with visually unique natural descriptions
or a clearly exhaustive image-level scope. Do not add facts, change the
operation, or change the answer. If unique reference cannot be
guaranteed, set safe_without_marks=false. Also generate three plausible
incorrect distractors in the same answer format.

Return JSON only:
{
"safe_without_marks": true,
"natural_question": "...",
"distractors": ["...", "...", "..."]
}
</pre>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompt B.8: Independent audit of the unmarked rewrite</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><pre id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
[UNMARKED ORIGINAL IMAGE]
Audit this visual question using only the unmarked original image.

Anchored source question: &lt;ANCHORED_QUESTION&gt;
Unmarked natural question: &lt;NATURAL_QUESTION&gt;

Independently answer the question and judge whether every reference or
exhaustive target set is uniquely determined. The question must require
multiple spatially separated regions. Ground each evidence area with a
box in normalized 0--1000 coordinates, locating it from pixels rather
than inferring it from wording. Also judge whether the rewrite preserves
the source task and whether every grounded area is required.

Return JSON only:
{
"answer": "...",
"reference_status": "unique | ambiguous",
"same_task_as_source": true,
"all_targets_identifiable": true,
"requires_multiple_regions": true,
"every_evidence_area_required": true,
"evidence_boxes": [
  {"description": "...", "bbox_2d": [x1,y1,x2,y2]}
],
"reason": "..."
}
</pre>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompt B.9: Multiple-choice distractor generation</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><pre id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
[MARKED ORIGINAL IMAGE]
You are given a visual question and its correct answer.

Original question: &lt;QUESTION&gt;
Correct answer: &lt;ANSWER&gt;

Generate three plausible but incorrect multiple-choice distractors.
Do not rewrite, paraphrase, simplify, or neutralize the question.
Keep the stem exactly unchanged. Distractors must be visually relevant,
distinct from the answer, and matched in answer format and approximate
length. For open-vocabulary answers, use concrete alternatives with the
same grammatical form and specificity. Do not use "none of the above,"
"all of the above," or "cannot be determined."

Return JSON only:
[{"distractors": ["d1", "d2", "d3"]}]
</pre>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompt B.10: Difficulty sampling on the policy view</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><pre id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
[POLICY VIEW: MARKED OR UNMARKED IMAGE]
Answer this multiple-choice visual question using only the image.

&lt;QUESTION_AND_OPTIONS&gt;

You may reason briefly before answering. The final answer must be:
&lt;answer&gt;X&lt;/answer&gt;

Rules:
- X must contain only A, B, C, or D.
- Do not output option text, coordinates, grounding tokens, or markers.
- Keep any reasoning to a few short sentences.
- The answer tag is required; otherwise the response is discarded.
</pre>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Training Data Statistics</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our training set contains 20.4K examples synthesized from SA-1B images by the pipeline in Section <a href="#S3" title="3 Boosting Multimodal Perception by Learning to Connect Visual Evidence ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Implementation Details ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>, and Figure <a href="#A3.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix C Training Data Statistics ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> summarizes its composition.
Each example involves three to seven regions, most often three (65.74%) or four (24.34%), followed by five (7.93%) and six or seven (1.99%).
The difficulty levels, defined by how many of the four screening responses are correct, are broadly distributed.
Specifically, easy, medium, hard, and very hard examples account for 33.75%, 22.04%, 19.07%, and 25.14% of the data, so more than 44% of the examples are hard or very hard.
Very hard examples, which the screening model never answers correctly, are kept, since their reference answers have already been anchored by two stronger VLMs.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F7" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.37037v1/data.svg" id="A3.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/278;" width="548" height="278"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7: </span>Composition of the 20.4K training examples by the number of selected regions per example and by difficulty level.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Training Details</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All models are trained with the same GRPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2024</a>)</cite> configuration for two epochs, with a batch size of 128 and a learning rate of <math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For each prompt, we sample <math id="A4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G{=}8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G{=}8</annotation></semantics></math> rollouts at temperature 0.7 with a maximum response length of 32K tokens, and the thinking mode is disabled during rollouts to keep responses concise.
We use decoupled clipping ratios <math id="A4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{\mathrm{low}}{=}0.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>low</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{\mathrm{low}}{=}0.2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{\mathrm{high}}{=}0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>high</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{\mathrm{high}}{=}0.3</annotation></semantics></math>, as proposed in DAPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and remove the KL penalty (<math id="A4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{\mathrm{KL}}{=}0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>KL</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{\mathrm{KL}}{=}0</annotation></semantics></math>), so that the policy is not anchored to the base model.
Finally, the reward checks whether the predicted option letter matches the ground-truth option.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Attention Map Coverage Analysis</h2>

<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation setting.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare ZwZ2-4B/9B with their Qwen3.5 base models on the same 405 TreeBench examples.
Within each scale, both checkpoints use the base-model processor and identical image–question pairs, visual-token grids, and evidence annotations.
Since Qwen3.5 interleaves linear-attention and full-attention layers, we evaluate all eight full-attention layers,
<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}=\{4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}=\{4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32\}</annotation></semantics></math> (1-based).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Attention extraction.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each example, we apply the chat template with the generation prompt and perform a single forward pass in evaluation mode using eager attention, without generating an answer.
We extract attention from the final token of this complete input sequence to the image tokens.
This position predicts the first answer token, so its attention indicates where the model looks as it begins to answer.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the visual-token indices for example <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> be its final input-token position.
For model <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> at layer <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, let
<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{i,\ell,h}^{m}(q_{i},v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{i,\ell,h}^{m}(q_{i},v)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the attention weight returned by head <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> to visual token <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math>.
We convert the extracted weights to float32, average equally over all <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{heads}}^{m,\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>n</mi><mi>heads</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{heads}}^{m,\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> heads, and then renormalize within the image tokens:</p>
<table id="A5.E1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="A5.E1X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.E1X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle u_{i,\ell}^{m}(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle u_{i,\ell}^{m}(v)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.E1X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{heads}}^{m,\ell}}\sum_{h=1}^{n_{\mathrm{heads}}^{m,\ell}}T_{i,\ell,h}^{m}(q_{i},v)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msubsup><mi>n</mi><mi>heads</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msubsup></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msubsup><mi>n</mi><mi>heads</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msubsup></munderover></mstyle><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{heads}}^{m,\ell}}\sum_{h=1}^{n_{\mathrm{heads}}^{m,\ell}}T_{i,\ell,h}^{m}(q_{i},v),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A5.E1Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.E1Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle a_{i,\ell}^{m}(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle a_{i,\ell}^{m}(v)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.E1Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{u_{i,\ell}^{m}(v)}{\sum_{v^{\prime}\in V_{i}}u_{i,\ell}^{m}(v^{\prime})}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><msubsup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{u_{i,\ell}^{m}(v)}{\sum_{v^{\prime}\in V_{i}}u_{i,\ell}^{m}(v^{\prime})}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.3" class="ltx_p">This renormalization over image tokens is applied once after head averaging, without renormalizing each head separately or applying an additional softmax.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evidence mask.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The visual tokens form an <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{i}\times W_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{i}\times W_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> grid for an image of size
<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{i}^{\mathrm{img}}\times W_{i}^{\mathrm{img}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>img</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>img</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{i}^{\mathrm{img}}\times W_{i}^{\mathrm{img}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
An annotated box <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{0},y_{0},x_{1},y_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{0},y_{0},x_{1},y_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> covers columns
<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\lfloor x_{0}W_{i}/W_{i}^{\mathrm{img}}\rfloor,\lceil x_{1}W_{i}/W_{i}^{\mathrm{img}}\rceil)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌊</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>/</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>img</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌋</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌈</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>/</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>img</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌉</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\lfloor x_{0}W_{i}/W_{i}^{\mathrm{img}}\rfloor,\lceil x_{1}W_{i}/W_{i}^{\mathrm{img}}\rceil)</annotation></semantics></math>
and the analogous row range, clipped to the grid boundaries.
This range includes every visual-token cell that overlaps the box.
The evidence set <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{i}\subseteq V_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{i}\subseteq V_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the union of the tokens covered by all annotated boxes, counting overlapping tokens once.
All evaluated examples have <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|E_{i}|&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|E_{i}|&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Top-<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> evidence IoU.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each example, we set <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{i}=|E_{i}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{i}=|E_{i}|</annotation></semantics></math> and select the <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> visual tokens with the largest head-averaged weights <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{i,\ell}^{m}(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{i,\ell}^{m}(v)</annotation></semantics></math> to form <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{i,\ell}^{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{i,\ell}^{m}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Ranking by the normalized weights <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i,\ell}^{m}(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i,\ell}^{m}(v)</annotation></semantics></math> gives the same ordering because the normalization divides all weights by a common positive value.
Ties are broken by visual-token index in row-major order, so exactly <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens are selected even when ties occur at the boundary.
Because <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is fixed by the annotation, the base and trained models receive the same token budget.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">With <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{i,\ell}^{m}=|A_{i,\ell}^{m}\cap E_{i}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo>∩</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{i,\ell}^{m}=|A_{i,\ell}^{m}\cap E_{i}|</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute</p>
<table id="A5.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{IoU}_{i,\ell}^{m}=\frac{|A_{i,\ell}^{m}\cap E_{i}|}{|A_{i,\ell}^{m}\cup E_{i}|}=\frac{h_{i,\ell}^{m}}{2k_{i}-h_{i,\ell}^{m}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>IoU</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo>∩</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo>∪</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{IoU}_{i,\ell}^{m}=\frac{|A_{i,\ell}^{m}\cap E_{i}|}{|A_{i,\ell}^{m}\cup E_{i}|}=\frac{h_{i,\ell}^{m}}{2k_{i}-h_{i,\ell}^{m}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.2" class="ltx_p">The score lies in <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, with larger values indicating better spatial alignment with the annotated evidence.
Since <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|A_{i,\ell}^{m}|=|E_{i}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|A_{i,\ell}^{m}|=|E_{i}|</annotation></semantics></math>, precision equals recall,
<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=h_{i,\ell}^{m}/k_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=h_{i,\ell}^{m}/k_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the IoU equals <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p/(2-p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p/(2-p)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Aggregation and layer-wise results.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We take the unweighted mean of the per-example IoU over the <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=405" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>405</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=405</annotation></semantics></math> paired examples, rather than pooling intersections and unions, and report differences in percentage points:</p>

<tbody>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.E3X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\operatorname{IoU}_{i,\ell}^{m}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover></mstyle><msubsup><mi>IoU</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\operatorname{IoU}_{i,\ell}^{m},</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A5.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Aggregation and layer-wise results. ‣ Appendix E Attention Map Coverage Analysis ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> shows gains in 7 of 8 layers at 4B and 6 of 8 layers at 9B.
The exceptions, layer 28 at 4B and layers 8 and 12 at 9B, each decrease by less than 0.03 percentage points.
These comparisons describe changes in sample means.
The metric measures spatial alignment at the final prompt position, rather than total attention mass or answer correctness.</p>

<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Case Study</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To complement the quantitative evaluation, we examine three selected examples in which ZwZ2-4B answers correctly while its base model, Qwen3.5-4B, fails.
Figure <a href="#A6.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Structured visual counting. ‣ Appendix F Case Study ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> presents examples from MIMIC, ZoomBench, and CountQA, covering cross-image category identification, spatially specified text recognition, and object counting.
We analyze the models’ visible responses to identify how their answers differ in the use of visual evidence and the satisfaction of question constraints.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cross-image consistency.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In Figure <a href="#A6.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Structured visual counting. ‣ Appendix F Case Study ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>(a), the MIMIC question asks for a category that appears in all five images.
The base model selects <em id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">wine glass</em>, even though its response explicitly acknowledges that this object is absent from some images.
It justifies the answer by referring to the most prominent shared item across the majority of the set, effectively replacing the requirement of universal presence with majority overlap.
ZwZ2 checks candidate categories against the full set of images.
Its response rules out <em id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">wine glass</em> because it is absent from Images 4 and 5, and identifies <em id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">person</em> as the category shared by all five images.
This example illustrates the importance of preserving the question’s scope when integrating evidence across images: an object shared by several images does not necessarily satisfy a constraint over the entire set.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Question-conditioned text localization.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A6.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Structured visual counting. ‣ Appendix F Case Study ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>(b) asks for the black text above the lower archway.
The base model recognizes the word <em id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">SEGATORI</em> on the adjacent building, but associates the question with inscriptions on the fountain and ultimately selects <em id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">FONTE</em>.
Its response therefore reveals a mismatch between the recognized text and the region specified by the question.
ZwZ2 identifies the entrance of the yellow building as the relevant lower archway and reads the sign immediately above it, yielding the correct answer, <em id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">SEGATORI</em>.
The case highlights the role of spatial reference resolution in visual text understanding: recognizing a visible word must be accompanied by establishing whether it belongs to the queried location.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Structured visual counting.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In Figure <a href="#A6.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Structured visual counting. ‣ Appendix F Case Study ‣ Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>(c), the CountQA question asks for the number of tablets in a blister pack.
The base model divides the image into regions above and below the yellow rubber band, reports two and four tablets, respectively, and returns <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2+4=6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2+4=6</annotation></semantics></math>.
Its arithmetic is consistent with these counts, so the error lies in enumerating the tablets.
ZwZ2 describes the pack as two columns and five rows, counts five tablets in each column, and obtains the correct total of <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5+5=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5+5=10</annotation></semantics></math>.
Here, the response uses the regular spatial arrangement to account for the complete set of tablets.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Together, these cases reflect the steps of connecting evidence: integrating facts over the full set of images in (a), binding recognized text to the queried location in (b), and accounting for every instance before aggregating in (c).</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.37037v1/case_study_three_positive.png" id="A6.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:548/617;" width="548" height="617" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8: </span>
<span id="A6.F8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Qualitative comparisons between Qwen3.5-4B and ZwZ2-4B.</span>
Three selected examples show correct predictions by ZwZ2-4B where the base model fails:
(a) identifying a category present in every image;
(b) associating recognized text with the queried location;
and (c) counting all instances in a structured arrangement.
Responses are excerpted from the original outputs, with omissions marked by <span id="A6.F8.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">[...]</span> and answer fields reformatted.
The enlarged image region in (b) is provided for visualization only.
</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Limitations and Future Work</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our work has two main limitations.
First, although our single-image supervision transfers to multi-image and agent tasks, it does not directly model temporal or cross-frame dependencies, so extending the synthesis to evidence spread across video frames is a natural next step.
Second, we apply RLVR to models of up to 27B parameters, and whether the same supervision benefits larger models or earlier training stages, such as pre-training, remains to be studied.</p>
</div>
</section>
</article>
</div>
